title: Shifting from knowledge retrieval to evidence exploration and synthesis - Nature Machine Intelligence
gist: Subscription preview of a News & Views piece by AstraZeneca and Turbine authors: only a two-sentence standfirst is available, arguing biomedical discovery is now bottlenecked by evidence integration rather than data, and highlighting DeepEvidence, a deep research agent that builds explicit representations of scientific evidence instead of just retrieving facts.

themes.theme: Evidence synthesis as the biomedical bottleneck

insights.claim: The limiting resource in biomedical discovery is no longer data but the ability to integrate and interpret evidence.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Shifts value in AI-for-drug-discovery from data generation toward evidence-integration and reasoning tools.
insights.quote: Biomedical discovery has entered an era in which the limiting resource is no longer data, but our ability to integrate and interpret evidence.
insights.locator: Biomedical discovery has entered an era

insights.claim: DeepEvidence, a new deep research agent, goes beyond retrieving facts by constructing explicit representations of scientific evidence, marking a shift from answer-centric systems to organizing evidence.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Next-generation research agents compete on structured evidence graphs, not chat answers, relevant to pharma R&D tooling.
insights.quote: DeepEvidence, a new deep research agent, goes beyond retrieving facts and constructs explicit representations of scientific evidence.

insights.claim: The commentary on evidence-synthesis agents is authored by researchers from AstraZeneca Oncology R&D and Turbine Simulated Cell Systems, indicating big-pharma and AI-biotech interest in this class of tools.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Pharma R&D teams are actively evaluating deep-research agents for target identification.
